Ok, so I've recently been watching A LOT of online videos on the Mandela Effect. Too many to link too. (most are good, some are... not)

Honestly it started here, on voat. Someone posted something about the Berenstain Bears... but I VERY VIVIDLY remember Berenstein Bears. I didn't think much of it at the time. I just thought maybe they got a misprint, or maybe they printed different spellings to different areas. Or had gone through a trademark dispute and had to change the spelling of the name for whatever reason... either way I shrugged it off for the time being.

This topic has resurfaced but with way too many differences that I just can't shrug off anymore. Over all the vids I've watched there's a lot of name brand things that seem to have changed over the years. I've noticed some as time has gone by but just thinking they were "re-branding" or have had some legal reasons for having to change their name. Come to find out "They've always been that way".

I've come up with a list of the ones that I can 100% "remember".

The first being:

  • Berenstein Bears.

I remember as a kid this being the same as Frankenstein or Einstein, as those names are not common in my area.

  • STAR WARS!

"Luke, I am your father" even James Earl Jones remembers it that way. I guess he now says "No, I am your father".

C3P0 having a silver leg in the original 3 movies?!?! He was ALWAYS completely gold.

  • Mister Rogers Theme Song

"It's a beautiful day in THE neighborhood" but I guess he's only talking about his own now. "It's a beautiful day in THIS neighborhood"

  • Snow White and the 7 Dwarfs

"Mirror mirror on the wall" I guess it's really just "Magic mirror on the wall"

  • Forest Gump

"Life IS like a box of chocolates" it's really "Life WAS like a box of chocolates"

  • Apollo 13 (the movie)

"Huston we HAVE a problem" but is "Huston we HAD a problem"

  • Coca-Cola

I remember the logo being"Coca~Cola" but I guess it's always been more along the lines of "Coca`Cola"

  • KitKat

I always remember Kit-Kat

  • Febreze

When did they drop the E? "Febreeze" is how I remember it.

  • Oscar Mayer

The second name is MEYER!

There was NEVER a space between the V and W

What's up the the "male" symbol? It was always just a circle.

I never remember it having that weird loopy thing on the end of the "F"

The Mandela Effect list goes on and on, but these are the only ones (currently) I can verify 100% for myself. Now I've heard a few different reasons for why this is happening, and the main stream reasoning are commonly vague (if not just out right saying you're crazy or need to lay off the drugs).

Alright, to those of you who are wondering if this works or not and are considering it - according to the YouTube channel's responses, no, it does not.

Now why, tribblepuncher, do you think anyone with half a brain might try this? Have you finally punched a tribble or two too many? Many years ago, my friend, but let me explain.

The technology industry is a very, very big fan of using the exact same stuff in different ways. One example of this is an old IBM card reader that could be upgraded by an IBM tech with a screw driver opening it up, turning a belt around, and closing it again. Another example is in the Intel 486. The original 486 had the first built-in floating-point unit (FPU) for x86 CPUs. However, competitors were offering a 486-like chip for less money because it had no FPU. So Intel split up the product line into DX (with FPU) and SX (without FPU). And for the SX's, instead of having a brand new die, they simply cut the controls to the FPU from the rest of the CPU, which means that most 486 SX chips have a perfectly good FPU rotting in there, never to actually be used. They may have changed this in later revisions of the silicon, but probably not. A more recent example is the Intel Core Solo, which was the only member of the Core line that was inherently single processor. They just took a Core Duo chip and cut the lines to one of the processors. Now in this case they may well have been able to use this to increase chip yields (if one core was defective but the other one wasn't, great way to recoup what would otherwise be a loss), but still, the point remains, and if they had to fill more orders than they had half-defective chips, some of the perfectly good Duos had one of their perfectly good cores cut.

This happens in software, too - there are a lot of Windows options buried deep in the registry that can cause different behavior by editing it, but there are no direct controls for it. In fact, there have been a number of software packages devoted to customizing Windows by using these very tweaks - even Microsoft got in the act for quite a few versions of Windows. So, leaving things in that make the unit multi-purpose is far from unheard of, and even though it's somewhat less common in hardware (particularly if it requires specific parts, e.g. a dedicated chip), it does indeed happen, and it is not out of the question that Apple may have included analog-to-digital circuitry in one of the chips and the basic leads to make a headphone jack theoretically possible.

So it is not a surprise that maybe Apple was using a board that still had components in there from the original stereo jack. It would be simple and relatively inexpensive to redesign to simply remove the jack, so the leads could still be sitting there, waiting for a signal that will never come. For all we know the boards are used on some other project that we know nothing of that indeed has a headphone jack, and as such they simply show their "courage" by not including the adapter.

Now, once again, this does not work according to the comments on the YouTube channel. But it is not unreasonable to believe that there just might have been a way to set this sort of thing up after all. I doubt most people who tried this really thought this much about it, but still, it's not completely unwarranted.

DISCLAIMER: Myself, unless I was 100% sure, and desperate for a headphone jack, I wouldn't do it, too many things you can get wrong drilling into random electronics. YMMV.

If it is a simulation, then you'd be asking yourself: "Are there other Universes, and if yes, are they all simulations as well?". If the answer is no to either question, then you have a serious dilemma.

If there are no other Universes, and ours is the only one, it would mean that the Universe was created artificially or only one Universe can exist at any given moment. However, if multiple Universes exist, but they are not simulations – then you must ask yourself: "Why is our Universe the only one that's a hologram?", which would lead you back to: "Is our Universe an artificially created one or can only one exist at any given time?"
